challenge_log.in_window: 23846280 is the only ChallengeState item in [22465639, 23874746), the period 0x9c79e8f5 (LAYER_2_CHAIN_ID = 1) was the implementation; it precedes the 2818 redeploy by 28466 blocks. The next one, 23874907, is 161 blocks after the redeploy. The index's logs in [23846280, 23874746] are 1 ChallengeState, 158 CommitBatch, 39 FinalizeBatch and 1 Upgraded.

chain_id_check.use_at_v0_4_3: Rollup.sol at v0.4.3 (V6) reads LAYER_2_CHAIN_ID in two places: the public getter, and _verifyProof (line 618), where it is the first field of abi.encodePacked(LAYER_2_CHAIN_ID, prevStateHash, postStateHash, withdrawRootHash, sequencerSetVerifyHash, dataHash, blobVersionedHash); the keccak256 of that is _publicInputHash, passed to IRollupVerifier(verifier).verifyAggregateProof(version, batchIndex, proof, publicInputHash). _verifyProof is called only from proveState, in the branch where the challenge has not timed out (line 500: the defender's proof). commitBatch, finalizeBatch and challengeState do not read it. So while 0x9c79e8f5 was live, a defender's proof was checked against a public input hash that commits to chain id 1. What the verifier contract then accepts is not in the evidence.

how_the_challenge_ended.direct_evidence: none in the repository or in I59's index. I59 fetched five topics (CommitBatch, RevertBatch, FinalizeBatch, ChallengeState, Upgraded: spec/M2/lib/historical.json), not ChallengeRes, Paused or Unpaused. Its index items keep only topic 0, block, log index, tx and sha256s, so the challenged batch index and challenger are not in it either; I59's raw snapshot (/root/.holon/historical) is not present in this container. git grep finds no other mention of block 23846280 or its tx in the repository.
how_the_challenge_ended.what_the_evidence_rules_out: From I59's index plus V6's code (v0.4.3; both implementations live from 22465639 to 24575030 are V6): (1) a ChallengeState item exists at 23874907, and challengeState requires !inChallenge, revertReqIndex == 0 (nonReqRevert) and not paused; (2) in V6, inChallenge is cleared only by proveState (either branch), revertBatch (which emits RevertBatch) and setPause(true); revertReqIndex is set only by the timeout branch of proveState (_challengerWin, to the batch index, which is >= 1) and cleared only by revertBatch; (3) I59 fetched RevertBatch over the whole window and found 0 (docs/iterations/I59.md, Counts); (4) the 23874746 upgrade receipt holds only the proxy's Upgraded log and one log of the executing account 0xf101f7f5, with no Initialized and no proxy state event. So by block 23874907 the 23846280 challenge had ended, neither by a challenger win on timeout nor by revertBatch. That leaves proveState with a proof the verifier accepted (a defender win), or setPause(true) (deposit refunded, challenge deleted) followed by setPause(false).
how_the_challenge_ended.not_determinable_here: which of those two; when; and, if by proof, whether it ran under 0x9c79e8f5 (chain id 1, before 23874746) or under 0xdf0749e6 (2818, in the 161 blocks before 23874907). Reading ChallengeRes (topic 0xe70d3820e244d5f71d1a6395db24f3460e8dca966edc1fd3625b6292880a877a = keccak256("ChallengeRes(uint256,address,string)")) or Paused/Unpaused on chain would decide it. I deliberately did not query it, because it lies outside the repository and the index and could bear on I28's prereg.

findings.where: holon/frontends/solidity/history.py:439 (_index), used by fetch, fetch --check and timeline
findings.what: holon accepts the upgrade source by its self-declared index_sha256 field and never recomputes the content hash. In a scratch copy I replaced results/M2/historical/index.json with a 9 KB file holding only the 12 Upgraded and 12 receipt items plus the declared field (recomputed content hash fec0e761.., pin d12801b7..). `history fetch --check` and `history timeline --check` both exited 0.
findings.why: The contract's Inputs define the source as the file whose recomputed content hash is upgrades.index_sha256, and a stale input is exit 2. Receipts are anchored only through that index, so holon's own --check is weaker than the contract. No outcome changes, and the suite still catches a doctored index: TestInstrument.test_the_index_is_i59s recomputes the hash. But TestOnchain.test_fetch_check_reproduces_offline alone would pass on one.
findings.fix: In _index, recompute sha256(json.dumps(doc without index_sha256, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False)) and raise Refused on a mismatch (a few seconds on 136 MB).

findings.what: Only Refused and ExtractionError are mapped to exit codes. Anything else escapes as a traceback with Python's exit 1, the code the contract reserves for '--check differs'. In a scratch copy, a sidecar without 'target' exits 1 with KeyError. Other paths that escape: subprocess.TimeoutExpired from solc or git, and OSError on a write. Also, `int(args[0]['value'], 0)` raises ValueError on a valid number literal that is not a plain integer (e.g. reinitializer(1e0)). The instrument records that as the ref's error and continues; holon aborts the whole extract.
findings.why: Exit-code contract: 1 only for --check differs; 2 for a refused input; 3 for an extraction error. On that literal holon and the instrument would diverge. No current input triggers any of these.
findings.fix: Catch ValueError in initializers as ExtractionError, and at the CLI boundary map KeyError/TypeError on the sidecar to 2 and other exceptions (timeouts, OSError) to 3.

findings.what: fetch --check does not compare the snapshot's proxy, window and rpc fields with the sidecar, and does not flag stray files in receipts/ or code/. No test checks these fields either.
findings.why: An edited proxy or window in onchain.json would still --check. The committed values are correct: I checked proxy, window, rpc host and methods against the sidecar, and all 12 block times against the prereg's table.
findings.fix: Compare these fields (and the file sets) in check_snapshot.

findings.where: contract H2/H7 (code identity zeroes immutables); results/M3/history/timeline.json blocks 22465639 and 23874746
findings.what: By design, the outputs cannot show that V6 was deployed with LAYER_2_CHAIN_ID = 1 at 22465639 and redeployed with 2818 at 23874746. The timeline shows V6 -> V6, consistent, nothing introduced. For about 6.5 months (2025-05-12 to 2025-11-25) the proxy's defender-proof public input committed to chain id 1, and one ChallengeState (23846280) fell in that period.
findings.why: This is a behavioural difference between two deployments of one version, and I28's versioned machines will inherit it. The extracted model already takes the value as a parameter (HEnv.e_immutable_LAYER_2_CHAIN_ID). The M3 model's init file uses 0xcf55 (53077), from a test-harness replay, which is neither mainnet value.
findings.fix: State it under Surprises in docs/iterations/I63.md, and key a deployment by (version, immutable words) in I28. No change to I63's contract or outputs.

findings.what: Cheap explanation of the unmatched implementation: v0.4.0's Rollup.sol with its line 181 deleted, `require(finalizedStateRoots[0] == bytes32(0), "genesis batch imported");` (the guard of importGenesisBatch). Built under hardhat (runs 10000, cancun, bytecodeHash none, pinned solc and deps), it reproduces the deployed runtime code byte for byte: 17900 bytes, both immutable words 2818, the same CBOR tail. The same edit under runs 200 or 999999 does not match. The code has the same 46 dispatcher selectors as V3's deployment and lacks V4's initialize2(bytes32) and committedStateRoots(uint256). This fits I59's report of two importGenesisBatch calls (20999915 and 21007528) on either side of this upgrade. In the local clone's 208 refs, the guard string's count in Rollup.sol changes in exactly one commit, 9f839c3f (2024-05-10, which added it), so no reachable commit removes it. That fact was obtained by the command described under review_process_incident.
findings.why: It explains the coverage debt (an uncommitted one-line variant of V3) without smoothing it over. The layout equals V3's, and the variant has only `initialize`, which was already consumed at 20998835, so P5's reasoning is unaffected.
findings.fix: Report it as coverage debt with this explanation. Do not add the variant to the basis; the basis is fixed.

findings.what: holon reads the source unit as raw bytes decoded as UTF-8, while the instrument uses read_text, which translates CRLF and CR to LF. A source with CR bytes would get a different source_sha256 and possibly different line numbers.
findings.why: Latent only: none of the 26 pinned refs' Rollup.sol contains a CR byte (checked), and the outputs equal the basis.
findings.fix: None needed for I63. If the contract is reused, say which text is hashed.

review_process_incident.what: My own breach of the review's constraints, not a build finding. At about 16:58 UTC I ran `git log --all -S'"genesis batch imported"' -- contracts/contracts/l1/rollup/Rollup.sol` in /root/work/morph without a no-fetch guard, to check whether any commit removed the guard. The clone is partial (remote.origin.promisor=true, partialclonefilter=blob:none), so git lazily fetched the missing historical Rollup.sol blobs from https://github.com/morph-l2/morph, a host outside the allowed set (it is the target repository's own origin, not scroll-tech). It then ran `git gc --auto` in the background ('Auto packing the repository in background', printed 11 times).
review_process_incident.effects: In /root/work/morph/.git: all 56 files under objects/pack now date from 16:58:47-53 (one 49 MB repacked promisor pack plus about 13 small promisor packs of fetched blobs), and packed-refs, logs/HEAD, refs/heads and objects/info were rewritten. The working tree and the index file are untouched (index mtime 2026-10-15). Nothing under /home/user/HOLON-i61b was written.
review_process_incident.integrity_checked_after: tests_m3._i63.refs() still equals the basis's 26 refs (25 pinned tags and head); HEAD is 3e44e795; extract run twice afterwards is byte-identical to the committed history; .git/info/refs is dated 16:38:31, before this review started.
review_process_incident.containment: Every later git call ran with GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file, gc.auto=0 and maintenance.auto=false. One later lazy-fetch attempt (from `git show -s 9f839c3f`) was refused ('transport https not allowed'), and the pack count stayed at 56.
review_process_incident.information_obtained: Only the commit list in finding B5 (one commit, 9f839c3f, changes the guard string's count). No prediction depends on it.
review_process_incident.action_for_lead: Disclose it in docs/iterations/I63.md: a network fetch from the target's GitHub origin, and a rewrite of the target checkout's object store, during the build review.
